Five models of Apple Watch can measure your blood pressure so as to issue warnings about possible high blood pressure, but they won't provide actual blood pressure readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but they need to be calibrated periodically with a traditional cuff-style blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to provide full blood pressure measurement results without any calibration, and says that the results of a trial involving thousands of people support its claim...

"Silent killer"

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) can both pose significant risks to health.

Of the two, high blood pressure is the more dangerous, commonly known as the "silent killer", because it can cause serious and irreversible damage to the arteries, heart and brain without any obvious symptoms. The condition often goes undetected until it triggers a heart attack or stroke.

Especially for the elderly, regular blood pressure monitoring is very important, and household cuff-style blood pressure monitors are available on the market for convenient self-measurement. However, it would of course be more ideal if fully automatic monitoring could be done through a fitness device you wear daily.

Apple Watch blood pressure function

With the launch of watchOS 26, five models of Apple Watch can measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models won't provide any readings — they'll only alert you when signs of possible high blood pressure are detected. Other devices like the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

There are indeed some fitness devices on the market that can provide actual blood pressure readings, but they must be calibrated periodically with measurements from a cuff-style blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup company Vital Signals says it has developed a smart ring — the Signal Ring — that can measure blood pressure as accurately as a traditional upper-arm cuff blood pressure monitor without any calibration.

According to Bloomberg, the company's CEO Tom Moss revealed that he himself had nearly died from undiagnosed high blood pressure, and subsequently founded the company.

The Signal Ring begins taking pre-orders later today, ships in October, and is priced at US$399 with no subscription required. Real-time blood pressure readings and long-term tracking data can be displayed through a companion app (see image above).

It's worth noting that the Oura Ring has not yet obtained marketing authorisation from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials show that the ring can provide accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss has no intention of marketing this ring to all consumers. He says its specialist functionality is best suited to the elderly, as well as people assessed by doctors as being at risk of high blood pressure — implying that the Signal Ring is average when it comes to other aspects such as sleep tracking.
